WITH
  movie_companies_ru AS (
    SELECT mc.*
    FROM movie_companies AS mc
    JOIN company_name AS cn ON mc.company_id = cn.id AND cn.country_code = '[ru]'
  ),
  cast_info_voice_uncredited AS (
    SELECT ci.*
    FROM cast_info AS ci
    WHERE ci.note LIKE '%(voice)%' AND ci.note LIKE '%(uncredited)%'
  ),
  char_name_actor AS (
    SELECT chn.*
    FROM char_name AS chn
    JOIN cast_info AS ci ON chn.id = ci.person_role_id
    JOIN role_type AS rt ON rt.id = ci.role_id
    WHERE rt.role = 'actor'
  ),
  title_movie AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.*
    FROM title AS t
    JOIN movie_companies_ru ON t.id = mc.movie_id
    LEFT JOIN cast_info_voice_uncredited ON t.id = ci.movie_id AND ci.id = cast_info_voice_uncredited.id
  )
SELECT MIN(chn.name) AS uncredited_voiced_character, MIN(t.title) AS russian_movie
FROM title_movie
JOIN char_name_actor ON char_name_actor.movie_id = title_movie.id
WHERE title_movie.id IS NOT NULL

    JOIN cast_info AS ci ON chn.id = ci.person_role_id
    JOIN role_type AS rt ON rt.id = ci.role_id
    WHERE rt.role = 'actor'
  ),
  title_movie AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.*
    FROM title AS t
    JOIN movie_companies_ru ON t.id = mc.movie_id
    LEFT JOIN cast_info_voice_uncredited ON t.id = ci.movie_id AND ci.id = cast_info_voice_uncredited.id
  )
SELECT MIN(chn.name) AS uncredited_voiced_character, MIN(t.title) AS russian_movie

This version of the query reduces the number of subqueries and joins the tables directly, which should improve performance. The `LEFT JOIN` is used to include all rows from the `title_movie` table even if there are no matching rows in the `cast_info_voice_uncredited` table. The filter `title_movie.id IS NOT NULL` ensures that only the rows with a match in the `cast_info_voice_uncredited` table are considered for the final result set.
